findings.text: follow-on: the correlation signature for a rate-limit or transport cause is sha256(kind, '', lowered_full_text) (reckon/crew/recovery.py:7140-7146), so two same-backend terminals of the same cause whose recorded text differs -- a reset time, a connection string -- carry different signatures and stay individual, reporting a genuine lane event as N worker failures. Reproduced on the reviewed head: two same-backend rate-limit terminals 4 s apart, text differing only in the reset time ('resets 10:40am' vs 'resets 11:15am'), read 2 abandoned / 0 lane events, while byte-identical text reads 1 lane event. Keying on the cause kind (and, for catalog changes, the model identity) rather than the full text would group the event without re-fusing unlike causes.

follow-on: `classified = classified_live or classify_pointer(record) if source == 'live' else {}` is precedence-dependent and falls back to ungrouped classification whenever classified_live is falsy, so a future caller passing an empty grouped list silently loses the lane-event grouping; an explicit `if source == 'live':` branch that distinguishes None from an empty list would remove the footgun.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 7fbe5fd8; 5fa8c4f7 adds LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS, _terminal_lane_signal and group_terminal_lane_events plus query.py wiring, 0df57957 adds the grouping test, 3b689808 adds the stderr negative test, 613aaef7 adds the evidence fragment, 4bd94f4b narrows the merge to a shared (backend, cause-signature) key and carries per-member recovery, 47ea0c3d updates the fragment only.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks that the grouping live in recovery.py and be reported once by the query.py fleet surfaces, with a test on temporary live pointers that fails at base; tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py drives project_live_rows, runs_view and recover, its ten cases fail at base 7fbe5fd8 (10 of the base arm's 11 failure ids are this file), pass at head, and the declared window=0 mutation reddens two of them (2 failed, 8 passed, EXIT=1); the four mixed-cause parametrizations and test_grouped_members_keep_their_own_resume_verdict reproduced the prior follow-ons at head 613aaef7 (4 failed, 5 passed, EXIT=1) before the repair commit 4bd94f4b.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's declared goal is that runs ending together on one backend are one lane event, not N worker failures; group_terminal_lane_events (reckon/crew/recovery.py:7149) now folds only terminals that share a recorded cause signature AND a backend within LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS, keyed on (backend, signature), and the repair carries each member's own recovery (resume only with a resolved session, a live worktree and a present session_id; else that member's own verb); wired at reckon/crew/query.py:172 and :479 and reckon/crew/recovery.py:10661; docked because the signature for rate-limit and transport causes still hashes the full terminal text, so the same cause recorded with differing wording (a reset time, a connection string) does not group and the lane event reports as N individual failures.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, six commits, both suites recorded as JSON with revisions, literal absolute-path commands and log paths, the negative-control log named and executed with revision and mutation declared, and the one remaining head failure declared as a base-existing follow-on outside this node's scope.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff base..head touches exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/query.py, tests/test_simultaneous_ends_are_one_lane_event.py and the done-when-named fragment docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/simultaneous-ends-are-one-lane-event.html, all inside the manifest's declared write paths; no file outside scope is modified and no plan or shared index is touched.

justifications.durability: the negative control removes LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS and reddens the grouping case and the per-member recovery case (2 failed, 8 passed, EXIT=1), the new tests drive the real entry points project_live_rows, runs_view and recover, the per-member resume-vs-recover decision is now asserted, and the repair's reproduction at the prior head is on disk; docked because the only mutation exercised is the window and no arm shows the shared-cause signature itself is load-bearing, so a regression that fused unrelated causes again would not redden any recorded test.
justifications.evidence: both arms are recorded at their own revision with literal absolute-path commands and completed true -- base 7fbe5fd8 11 failed/150 passed, head 4bd94f4b 1 failed/160 passed -- and head-minus-base over pytest node ids is empty so added_failure_count is 0; the negative-control log names its revision and mutation and ends EXIT=1; an independent focused run at the reviewed head read 1 failed/101 passed with only the base-existing test_cli_follow failure; docked because the base arm's tree carried the new test file that the base revision does not contain, so ten of its eleven failure ids are the reproduction rather than a clean base arm, and the head suite ran at 4bd94f4b, one docs-only commit below the reviewed head 47ea0c3d, so after_suite.revision is not reviewed_head_sha.
justifications.fit: group_terminal_lane_events, _terminal_lane_signal and LANE_EVENT_WINDOW_SECONDS extend the existing RECOVERY_CLASSES and RECOVERY_VERBS tables in place and follow the module's classify-then-group idiom with no plan label or version suffix; docked because the signature hashes the already-parsed lowered text rather than the structured (kind, model) fields it already carries, and because the precedence-dependent `classified_live or classify_pointer(record) if source == 'live' else {}` at reckon/crew/query.py:235 reads as a fallback-to-ungrouped footgun for a future falsy classified_live.
justifications.goal_fidelity: group_terminal_lane_events (reckon/crew/recovery.py:7149) plus the wiring at reckon/crew/query.py:172 and :479 and recover at reckon/crew/recovery.py:10661 deliver the declared goal for the recorded catalog-change cluster and keep unlike, absent and model-distinct causes individual, but the shared-cause signature for rate-limit and transport causes includes the full terminal text, so two runs of the same cause with differing wording stay individual (measured: two same-backend rate-limit terminals 4 s apart, differing reset text, read 2 abandoned / 0 lane events; identical text read 1 lane event), which leaves the section's own N-failures harm in place for those causes.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff spans exactly the four declared write paths and the fragment was named by the done-when, so nothing outside the granted scope was touched and no shared index or plan state was mutated.
